question.text: Which of the following is a valid reason for the RTA to reject a dematerialisation request?

answer.text: The details on the physical certificate do not match the electronic request submitted by the DP
The investor has less than 100 shares in the company
The investor holds shares in a company listed on a regional stock exchange
The investor has not completed one year of holding the physical certificates

explanation.text: The Logic: Per page 130, a mismatch between the information in the DRF/electronic request and the physical certificates is a listed reason for full or partial rejection of a demat request. Page 129 supports the DRF/DRN and certificate-verification checks that lead up to this rejection decision. The Trap: The other three options describe restrictions (minimum quantity, regional-exchange listing, minimum holding period) that are not listed in the source as grounds for rejection of a demat request. Note: The source rejection reasons centre on DRF/DRN/certificate verification failures rather than on quantity, listing venue, or holding period.
